geometry_source: EU5 calibrated location geometry plus cited historical maps, village descriptions and archaeological survey reports. All three records remain unresolved/validation-only; no partial selector is treated as an accepted aggregate target.

crosswalks.historical_boundary: The more-than-100 (project database: 124) villages and hamlets in the 1245 al-Nabulusi survey, connected by canal and water-right entries. QMUL's Fayyum map/database is a point/grid reconstruction, not a closed aggregate polygon.
crosswalks.boundary_confidence: medium for the named Fayyum point; low for the complete 124-village aggregate
crosswalks.resolution_method: Retain the Fayyum tag only as a candidate physical-feature join. Georeference the QMUL FayyumMap1 and Settlementtable grid, then intersect each village/canal record with calibrated EU5 polygons. Do not assign the eventual aggregate to the single candidate location before the area overlap is measured.
required_actions: map all village/canal records and explicitly account for unmapped area
obtain and audit the exact Rapoport Chapter 3 population table or interval
keep partial poll-tax heads and fiscal levies out of population targets
crosswalks.notes: The location selector is a candidate only. A named Fayyum location is not evidence that its EU5 polygon covers the historic 124-village boundary.

crosswalks.historical_boundary: Tulkarm waqf village and its agricultural lands on Wadi al-Sha'ir described in the 1354 waqf order. The reviewed article does not provide a georeferenced waqf polygon; its household/population numbers are from the 1535 and 1548 Ottoman administrative records.
crosswalks.resolution_method: Candidate name selector only. Reconstruct the 1354 waqf land boundary from the source's land description or an independent cadastral map, geocode Tulkarm/Wadi al-Sha'ir, and intersect with EU5 polygons. Keep the 1535/1548 household counts in a dated validation table, never as a 1354 target.
required_actions: locate or digitize the 1354 waqf boundary
verify the EU5 map tag for Tulkarm and report exact matched locations
separate 1354 land evidence from 1535/1548 Ottoman population evidence
find an independent 1354-compatible saturation/pressure interval before promotion
crosswalks.notes: The 95-household/approximately-522-person value is explicitly sourced to 940H/1535 AD in endnote 33. This crosswalk cannot make it a 1354 population label.

crosswalks.historical_boundary: Archaeological villages of Hubras and Saham and the agricultural/pastoral hinterlands surveyed in northern Jordan. Walker and the ADAJ report describe the survey unit but the scanned report does not supply a closed boundary polygon or a population count.
crosswalks.resolution_method: Candidate site-name selectors only. Obtain the survey site polygons/coordinates from Walker BASOR 339 and ADAJ 51, digitize the village-plus-hinterland extents, and calculate area-weighted overlap with calibrated EU5 locations. Preserve the late-fourteenth-century decline as a pressure diagnostic, not a population target.
required_actions: extract or digitize Hubras and Saham survey extents
resolve EU5 location aliases and exact matched count
retain the late-fourteenth-century productivity decline with political/market caveats
find a defensible two-sided people or capacity interval before any promotion
crosswalks.notes: No population interval is fabricated from the archaeological decline. The selectors are unresolved until the survey extents are mapped.
